CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 1) The usual site of fertilization is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The ampullary part of the fallopian tube is the commonest site of fertilization because it provides the optimum environment for fusion of sperm and ovum.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 2) The fertilizable life span of the ovum is approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The secondary oocyte remains capable of fertilization for about 12–24 hours after ovulation.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 3) The fertilizable life span of spermatozoa in the female genital tract is approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Most sperm remain capable of fertilization for about 2–3 days within the female reproductive tract.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 4) Implantation normally begins on which day after fertilization?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Implantation usually starts around the sixth day after fertilization when the blastocyst attaches to the endometrium.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 5) The commonest site of implantation is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.option3: Anterior or posterior wall near the uterine fundus
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Normal implantation occurs in the upper uterine cavity, usually on the anterior or posterior wall near the fundus.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 6) The pregnant endometrium is known as:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The endometrium undergoes decidual transformation after implantation and is then called the decidua.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 7) Human placenta is best described as:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Human placenta is discoid in shape, hemochorial in circulation, and deciduate because maternal decidua is shed at delivery.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 8) The fetal component of the placenta is formed by:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Chorion frondosum forms the fetal part of the placenta.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 9) The maternal component of the placenta is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Decidua basalis forms the maternal part of the placenta.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 10) Approximately how many cotyledons are present in a term placenta?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The maternal surface of a normal term placenta contains about 15–20 cotyledons.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 11) The principal cell layer responsible for secretion of hCG is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Syncytiotrophoblast secretes hCG and several other placental hormones.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 12) Which placental function is responsible for oxygen transfer from mother to fetus?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the placental membrane mainly by simple diffusion.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 13) Glucose crosses the placenta mainly by:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Glucose is transported across the placenta via GLUT-1-mediated facilitated diffusion.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 14) Amino acids are transported across the placenta primarily by:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Amino acids require active transport to meet fetal growth demands.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 15) Which hormone does not significantly cross the placenta?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Parathormone does not normally cross the placenta to any significant extent.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 16) Which enzyme is synthesized by the placenta?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Oxytocinase is one of the important enzymes synthesized by the placenta.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 17) The normal volume of amniotic fluid at term is approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: A normal term pregnancy contains approximately 600–800 mL of amniotic fluid.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 18) Meconium-stained amniotic fluid most commonly suggests:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Green meconium-stained liquor is classically associated with fetal distress, although it may occur in breech presentation.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 19) Golden-colored amniotic fluid is classically associated with:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Hemolysis in Rh isoimmunization may produce golden-yellow amniotic fluid.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 20) Polyhydramnios is diagnosed when the amniotic fluid index (AFI) is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Polyhydramnios is defined by an AFI greater than 25 cm or an amniotic fluid volume exceeding approximately 2 liters.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 21) The anatomical definition of polyhydramnios is amniotic fluid volume:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Polyhydramnios is defined anatomically as an amniotic fluid volume greater than 2000 mL at term.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 22) The commonest cause of polyhydramnios is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: About 50–60% of polyhydramnios cases are idiopathic.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 23) Polyhydramnios is commonly associated with which fetal anomaly?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Fetal swallowing is impaired in esophageal atresia, leading to polyhydramnios.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 24) Oligohydramnios is diagnosed when the amniotic fluid index (AFI) is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: An AFI below 5 cm is diagnostic of oligohydramnios.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 25) The anatomical definition of oligohydramnios is amniotic fluid volume:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Oligohydramnios is defined anatomically as less than 200 mL of liquor at term.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 26) Which fetal anomaly is classically associated with oligohydramnios?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Renal agenesis causes absent fetal urine production, resulting in severe oligohydramnios.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 27) The normal umbilical cord contains:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: A normal umbilical cord contains two umbilical arteries and one umbilical vein embedded in Wharton’s jelly.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 28) The gelatinous substance surrounding umbilical vessels is called:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Wharton’s jelly protects the umbilical vessels from compression.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 29) After birth, the umbilical vein becomes the:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The obliterated umbilical vein forms the ligamentum teres of the liver.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 30) After birth, the ductus arteriosus becomes the:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Functional closure of the ductus arteriosus is followed by fibrous transformation into the ligamentum arteriosum.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 31) The foramen ovale closes after birth to form the:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Closure of the foramen ovale leaves the fossa ovalis in the interatrial septum.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 32) Which placental hormone is primarily responsible for maintaining the corpus luteum in early pregnancy?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: hCG maintains the corpus luteum until placental hormone production becomes adequate.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 33) Placental hormonal function largely shifts from the corpus luteum at approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Around 6–8 weeks of gestation, the placenta assumes the primary endocrine role.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 34) Human chorionic gonadotropin is first detectable approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: hCG becomes detectable soon after implantation, approximately 8–9 days after fertilization.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 35) Markedly elevated β-hCG is classically seen in:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Trophoblastic proliferation in a hydatidiform mole produces very high β-hCG levels.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 36) Low serum β-hCG is most suggestive of:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: In ectopic pregnancy, β-hCG levels are typically lower than expected for gestational age and rise abnormally slowly.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 37) Which of the following is a presumptive sign of pregnancy?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Amenorrhea is a subjective (presumptive) sign and is not diagnostic of pregnancy.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 38) Goodell’s sign refers to:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.option3: Softening of the lower uterine segment
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Goodell’s sign is softening of the cervix due to increased vascularity during early pregnancy.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 39) Hegar’s sign refers to:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.option1: Softening of the lower uterine segment
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Hegar’s sign is softening and compressibility of the lower uterine segment in early pregnancy.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 40) The most reliable investigation for confirmation of an intrauterine pregnancy is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Ultrasonography directly demonstrates the gestational sac, yolk sac, or fetal pole and provides the most reliable confirmation of an intrauterine pregnancy.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 41) The earliest structure visible on transvaginal ultrasonography in a normal pregnancy is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The gestational sac is the earliest sonographic evidence of an intrauterine pregnancy.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 42) The first definitive evidence of an intrauterine pregnancy on ultrasound is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The yolk sac confirms a true intrauterine gestational sac and excludes a pseudogestational sac.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 43) Fetal cardiac activity is usually detected by transvaginal ultrasonography at approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Cardiac activity is generally visible by transvaginal ultrasound at 5–6 weeks of gestation.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 44) The normal duration of pregnancy, calculated from the first day of the last menstrual period (LMP), is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Pregnancy lasts about 280 days (40 weeks) from the first day of the LMP.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 45) Naegele’s rule is used to calculate the:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: EDD = First day of LMP + 1 year − 3 months + 7 days.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 46) Pregnancy calculated from the date of fertilization lasts approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Gestation from fertilization is approximately 266 days (38 weeks).

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 47) The fetal heartbeat is best heard by Doppler at approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Doppler ultrasound usually detects fetal heart sounds from 8–10 weeks onward.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 48) Fetal heart sounds are usually audible by a fetoscope at:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: A fetoscope generally detects fetal heart sounds after 18–20 weeks.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 49) Quickening is usually first perceived by a primigravida at:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Primigravidae usually perceive fetal movements around 18–20 weeks.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 50) Quickening is usually first perceived by a multiparous woman at:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Multiparous women often recognize fetal movements earlier due to previous experience.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 51) The normal fetal heart rate is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The normal baseline fetal heart rate ranges from 110 to 160 beats per minute.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 52) Which immunoglobulin crosses the placenta?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: IgG is actively transported across the placenta, providing passive immunity to the fetus.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 53) Which immunoglobulin does not cross the placenta?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: IgM is a large pentameric molecule and does not cross the placenta.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 54) The major source of amniotic fluid during the second half of pregnancy is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: After mid-pregnancy, fetal urine becomes the principal contributor to amniotic fluid volume.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 55) The primary mechanism for removal of amniotic fluid is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Fetal swallowing is the main route for removal of amniotic fluid.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 56) Which placental hormone has anti-insulin (diabetogenic) effects?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Human placental lactogen (hPL) increases maternal insulin resistance, ensuring glucose availability for the fetus.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 57) The placenta produces all of the following hormones except:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: FSH is secreted by the anterior pituitary, not the placenta.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 58) Which placental hormone is mainly responsible for breast development during pregnancy?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: hPL contributes to mammary gland growth and prepares the breasts for lactation.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 59) The umbilical vein carries:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.option1: Oxygenated blood from placenta to fetus
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.option2: Venous blood from fetus to mother
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.option3: Deoxygenated blood from fetus to placenta
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.option4: Mixed blood from placenta to fetus
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The single umbilical vein carries oxygenated, nutrient-rich blood from the placenta to the fetus.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 60) The umbilical arteries carry:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.option1: Deoxygenated blood from the fetus to the placenta
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The two umbilical arteries transport deoxygenated blood and metabolic waste from the fetus to the placenta for exchange.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 61) The fetal circulation bypasses the lungs primarily through the:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: These fetal shunts divert blood away from the non-functioning fetal lungs.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 62) Which fetal shunt connects the pulmonary artery to the descending aorta?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The ductus arteriosus allows most right ventricular output to bypass the lungs.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 63) Which fetal shunt connects the umbilical vein to the inferior vena cava?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The ductus venosus allows oxygenated blood from the placenta to bypass most of the liver.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 64) The organ responsible for fetal gas exchange is the:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The placenta functions as the fetal organ of respiration.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 65) The principal source of fetal oxygen is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Oxygen diffuses from maternal blood to fetal blood across the placental membrane.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 66) The placenta is completely formed by approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Structural and functional placental development is essentially complete by the end of the first trimester.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 67) The average weight of a term placenta is approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: A normal term placenta weighs about 500 g, approximately one-sixth of the fetal weight.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 68) The average diameter of a term placenta is approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: A mature placenta is discoid, measuring about 15–20 cm in diameter.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 69) The average thickness of a term placenta at its center is approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The normal placental thickness at term is about 2–3 cm.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 70) The fetal surface of the placenta is covered by:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The fetal surface is smooth and shiny because it is covered by the amnion.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 71) The maternal surface of the placenta appears:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The maternal surface is rough, dark red, and divided into 15–20 cotyledons.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 72) The umbilical cord normally inserts into the placenta:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Central or slightly eccentric insertion is the normal pattern.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 73) The average length of the umbilical cord at term is approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The normal umbilical cord measures approximately 50 cm at term.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 74) A single umbilical artery is most commonly associated with:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: A single umbilical artery is associated with an increased risk of congenital malformations and fetal growth restriction.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 75) Which placental hormone is chiefly responsible for maintaining uterine quiescence during pregnancy?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Progesterone suppresses uterine contractility and helps maintain pregnancy.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 76) The principal source of progesterone during the first few weeks of pregnancy is the:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Before the luteoplacental shift, progesterone is mainly secreted by the corpus luteum.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 77) The luteoplacental shift occurs at approximately:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Around 6–8 weeks, placental steroid production becomes sufficient to maintain pregnancy.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 78) The placenta synthesizes estrogen mainly from:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Placental estrogen production depends largely on dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEAS) from the fetal adrenal gland.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 79) The earliest physiological change suggesting pregnancy is usually:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Amenorrhea is typically the earliest clinical indication of pregnancy in women with regular menstrual cycles.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 80) The most accurate method for determining gestational age in the first trimester is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Crown-rump length measured in the first trimester provides the most accurate estimation of gestational age.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 81) The placenta acts as all of the following except:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The placenta performs respiratory, endocrine, nutritive, and excretory functions but is not the major hematopoietic organ throughout pregnancy.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 82) The most abundant immunoglobulin transferred from mother to fetus is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: IgG is actively transported across the placenta and provides passive immunity to the newborn.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 83) The placenta is expelled during which stage of labour?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The third stage of labour extends from delivery of the baby until expulsion of the placenta and membranes.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 84) The fetal membranes consist of:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: The fetal membranes are composed of the amnion internally and the chorion externally.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 85) Which of the following substances crosses the placenta mainly by simple diffusion?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the placenta mainly by simple diffusion.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 86) Which nutrient is transported across the placenta mainly by active transport?
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Amino acids are actively transported to meet the nutritional demands of the growing fetus.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 87) The principal physiological role of amniotic fluid is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.option4: To protect the fetus from trauma
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Amniotic fluid cushions the fetus, permits movement, and helps maintain a stable intrauterine environment.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 88) The fetus contributes to amniotic fluid by:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: After mid-pregnancy, fetal urine is the major contributor to amniotic fluid.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 89) The earliest hormone detected by pregnancy tests is:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: Pregnancy tests detect β-hCG, which is produced by the syncytiotrophoblast soon after implantation.

CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.question: 90) The physiological purpose of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) in early pregnancy is to:
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.option1: Maintain the corpus luteum and progesterone secretion
CONCEPTION, Fetoplacental unit, physiolo.exp: hCG preserves the corpus luteum during early pregnancy, ensuring continued progesterone production until the placenta assumes this role.
